summary.headline: Rupa & Company Q2 FY27 revenue flat at INR320.4 crores, but EBITDA rose 15.9% to INR26 crores on 8.1% margin.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was flat year-on-year at INR320.4 crores, against INR320.2 crores in Q2 FY26, amid a highly competitive market. EBITDA grew 15.9% to INR26 crores with margin up 110 bps to 8.1%, driven mainly by gross margin gains and lower advertising spend. PAT rose 17.4% to INR17 crores (5.3% margin). For H1 FY27, revenue grew 3.7% to INR522.8 crores and PAT grew 25.9% to INR25.3 crores. Management guided to around 10% revenue growth and around 9% EBITDA margin for H2 FY27.

segments.name: Athleisure
segments.commentary: Management said athleisure showed encouraging traction in the quarter and is being scaled up with focus on product mix. No separate revenue figure was disclosed.

segments.name: Thermal wear
segments.commentary: Thermal grew 30%+ YoY in Q2 FY27 per CFO; management expects better thermal performance through the year. No order book figure was given.

segments.name: Modern trade
segments.commentary: Modern trade contributed about 5% of overall business; INR25 crores of capex is earmarked for a dedicated warehouse for this channel.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27: hopeful of revenue growth of around 10% and EBITDA margin of around 9%, per Vikash Agarwal.
CFO confirmed on Q&A that H2 FY27 revenue target implies about INR880 crores, roughly 20% growth over H2 FY26 (about INR750 crores), when asked by an investor.
Management expects industry competition and margin pressure to ease in coming quarters, without quantifying timing.
Capex of about INR83 crores approved by Board, to be spent over 2 to 2.5 years.
capex_capacity: Board approved capex of about INR83 crores in total.
About INR58 crores for factory cum warehouse at West Bengal Hosiery Park.
About INR25 crores for warehouse and storage of accessories dedicated to modern trade.
Total outlay of INR83 crores to be spent over another 2 to 2.5 years.
No installed capacity or utilisation figures were discussed.
demand_pricing: Revenue was flat YoY in Q2 amid a highly competitive market.
Management described intense competition in hosiery: price war on schemes and discounts, and extended receivable credit days are a major challenge.
Competition intensity has not improved since last quarter, per CFO.
Management said the industry as a whole, including major brands, faces the issue; raw material prices are high.
Lux Industries' Q2 sales were cited by an investor as down about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA grow when revenue was flat?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to gross margin gain of about 30 bps, advertising cost falling to 4.7% of sales from 5.1%, and about 40 bps of savings in other expenses.

qa_highlights.question: What is Thermal growth and order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Thermal grew 30%+ in the quarter; management gave no order book figure and said Thermal should perform well through the year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the company move from debt-free to net borrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital rose by about INR75 crores from March 2026 to September 2026, so borrowings were increased to fund it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Board approved about INR83 crores: INR58 crores for a factory cum warehouse at West Bengal Hosiery Park and INR25 crores for a modern trade warehouse, over 2 to 2.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 10% growth guidance imply H2 sales of about INR880 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said yes, hopeful of achieving that, which is about 20% growth over H2 FY26 (about INR750 crores).

qa_highlights.question: Has competition intensity eased, and what is the longer-term margin view?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said intensity is unchanged from last quarter. Vikash Agarwal said the issue is industry-wide and expects improvement in coming quarters; no long-term margin target was given beyond the H2 9% guidance.

risks_watch: Price war, scheme and discount spending, and extended credit days in hosiery, affecting realisations and receivables.
H2 FY27 needs about 20% YoY revenue growth to meet the 10% full-year guide, against flat Q2 revenue.
Rising borrowings after working capital increased about INR75 crores since March 2026, ending the earlier debt-free position.
Raw material cost inflation cited by management.
Investor-noted shareholding reduction by Abakkus (about 4% to 2%); investor questioned margins versus the historical 13-14%.
summary.management_tone: Cautious on top line: management called the market highly competitive and revenue flat, while stressing margin gains and expecting industry conditions to improve. On the Q&A, the CFO answered yes/no and gave no quantified recovery timing.
key_quotes: The main reason for improvement in EBITDA is because of the improvement in gross margin.
Thermal showed a good traction during the quarter and registered a growth of 30% plus in this quarter.
It is not specific to us. This is like if you see the industry, industry is going through a little tough competitive time.
So I'm sure in coming quarters, things will improve.

growth.why: H2 FY27 guided to ~10% revenue growth (CFO implies ~INR880 crore vs ~INR750 crore, ~20%, which conflicts with the 10% figure) and ~9% EBITDA margin, but no order book, installed capacity or utilisation was given, and the new capex (INR83 crore, 2-2.5 years) only goes live in about 4+ quarters, so backing is vague while Q2 revenue was flat amid a price war.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin rose 110 bps to 8.1% on ~30 bps gross margin gain and advertising cut to 4.7% from 5.1%, and management guides ~9% EBITDA margin for H2 FY27 versus 8.0% in H1, though raw material inflation and price war are headwinds.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Board approved about INR83 crore (INR58 crore West Bengal factory-cum-warehouse, INR25 crore modern trade warehouse) to be spent over 2 to 2.5 years, so no new capacity goes live in the 2-4 quarter window; no installed capacity or utilisation was disclosed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management hopes for ~10% revenue growth in H2 (CFO: ~INR880 crore vs ~INR750 crore, ~20%), but Q2 revenue was flat at INR320.4 crore amid a price war, and no order book was given, so the gap is unproven.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Board has already approved about INR83 crore of capex; no utilisation figure was given, so no further capex announcement is signalled in the window.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held H2 guidance at ~10% growth and ~9% EBITDA margin only as 'hopeful', while Q2 revenue was flat and the CFO said competition intensity has not improved since last quarter.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 needs ~20% YoY revenue growth (about INR880 crore vs INR750 crore) to meet the 10% full-year guide against flat Q2, with industry price war, extended receivable days and raw material inflation cited.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Athleisure is being scaled up with encouraging traction and Thermal grew 30%+ YoY in Q2, but no specific launch dates or revenue figures were given.

rows.label: Shift from debt-free to net borrowing
rows.why: Working capital rose about INR75 crore from March 2026 to September 2026 and borrowings were raised to fund it, ending the debt-free position, with extended receivable credit days a stated challenge.

rows.label: Hosiery price war easing
rows.why: Management expects industry competition and margin pressure to ease in coming quarters without quantifying timing, but the CFO said intensity is unchanged from last quarter and Lux Industries' Q2 sales were down about 10%.

rows.label: Thermal wear momentum
rows.why: Thermal grew 30%+ YoY in Q2 FY27 and management expects better thermal performance through the year, but no order book figure was disclosed.

tone.note: Management was confident on margin gains (gross margin, lower advertising) and thermal growth but cautious on the flat top line amid a price war; analysts pressed on the ~20% H2 growth needed, the shift to net borrowing, and margins versus the historical 13-14%.
